maya: Quick thread — saw a p99 jump for model-x on g5 last night after the microbatch heuristic tweak. p95 mostly stable but tail doubled. CC @sam @jon

jon: Yep. p99 ~1.2s vs 600ms baseline. Stack shows more KV cache misses + kernel fallback thrash.

lee: Profiling dump:
```
[2026-03-17T23:12:01Z] req=0x3ff kernel=A qps=120 microbatch=8 seq=512 time_per_token=6.2ms
[2026-03-17T23:12:01Z] req=0x400 kernel=FALLBACK kernel=B cache=miss seq=512 time_per_token=11.8ms
[2026-03-17T23:12:02Z] req=0x401 kernel=A qps=120 microbatch=8 seq=64 time_per_token=2.1ms
[2026-03-17T23:12:02Z] req=0x402 kernel=FALLBACK kernel=B cache=miss seq=1024 time_per_token=14.5ms
```

maya: I tried reverting microbatch from 8 -> 4 on a canary host this morning. p99 improved to ~780ms but throughput dropped ~18%.

ara: FYI Sales: ACME asked for p95 120ms and p99 500ms flat. They're unhappy with 780ms.

sam: Options to present:
- revert the heuristic (instant fix, lowers throughput)
- KV prewarm + smarter cache (small code change, may help tail)
- kernel pinning for specific model_variants (trade memory for stable latency)
- per-customer SLO carveouts (Dedicated/reserved workers)

jon: Found a regression in kernel dispatch: during seq variance we binary-search kernel table and sometimes oscillate between kernels, causing extra copies. Repro in bench with mixed seq lengths.

lee: Patch idea: cache kernel selection per (model_version, hardware, seq_bucket) for 100-500ms. Avoids oscillation and fallback loops.

maya: Local bench results:
- baseline microbatch=8: p95=180ms p99=1200ms RPS=640
- microbatch=4 + kernel-cache: p95=140ms p99=430ms RPS=560 (-12%)
Promising tradeoff.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: staging -> canary: kernel-cache-ttl-100ms (build #4021)

sam: For ACME negotiations propose 2 tiers:
- Standard: p95 150ms / p99 600ms (hosted)
- Premium: p95 120ms / p99 450ms (Dedicated, reserved workers + kernel pinning)
Sale can sell Premium as SLA add-on.

ara: ACME explicitly said no throughput drop—we need to show the RPS delta for both tiers and cost delta.

maya: Action items:
- jon: run perf sweep (seq 16/64/256/512/1024) x microbatch [2,4,8] and produce CSV
- lee: prototype kernel-cache patch + bench on same sweep
- jon + maya: short 1-slide summary with numbers and recommended ask for Sales
Sync: tomorrow 10:30 PT. I'll post results before then.

jon: on it, attaching initial CSV in an hour.
